# Lovable says it added $100M in revenue last month alone, with just 146 employees

 Anna Heim 

2:40 PM PDT · March 11, 2026

Lovable crossed $400 million in annual recurring revenue in February, the Stockholm company confirmed to TechCrunch. But it declined to say whether it is still projecting to reach $1 billion ARR by year’s end, saying its focus is on “helping builders scale their impact with our platform.”

...

Also notable is the fact that Lovable achieved $400 million ARR with only 146 full-time employees, as chief revenue officer Ryan Meadows told Business Insider. The company now plans to increase its headcount — and there’s room for it. Its recently inaugurated space in Stockholm has space for 300 people, and the company is also hiring in Boston, London, New York, San Francisco, and remotely.

Even accounting for these 70 open positions, Lovable’s revenue-to-employee ratio will likely remain well above industry norms. Research firm Gartner predicts that a new wave of unicorns will emerge by 2030 with $2 million ARR per employee. At $2.77 million in ARR per employee, Lovable has already surpassed that number.

results.title: Lovable hit $500 million in revenue with 146 employees. Its new data shows who is actually building software now.
results.author: Alina Maria Stan
highlights:
Lovable hit $500 million in revenue with 146 employees. Its new data shows who is actually building software now.

This article was published on June 9, 2026

# Lovable hit $500 million in revenue with 146 employees. Its new data shows who is actually building software now.

80% of builders on the platform are non-technical. 720 million monthly visits to Lovable-built projects. 8 in 10 users plan to monetise. The “build economy” is the company’s bet that software creation is decoupling from coding.

...

#### TL;DR

Lovable published its first “build economy” report showing 80% of builders are non-technical, 720M monthly visits to projects, and 8 in 10 users plan to monetise. The company claims $500M ARR with 146 employees. Data is self-reported and unaudited.

Lovable, the Swedish vibe-coding platform that lets users build apps through natural language, has published its first data report on what it calls the “build economy.” The report draws on product usage data from January 2025 to May 2026, alongside a May 2026 user survey, and describes a shift in who builds software, what they build, and why.

The company says it has surpassed $500 million in annualised revenue run rate, up from $400 million in February, when it added $100 million in a single month with just 146 employees. That translates to roughly $2.77 million in ARR per employee, a figure that exceeds Gartner’s 2030 prediction for unicorns by four years.

...

### The caveats

Lovable’s data is self-reported and drawn from its own platform. The 80% non-technical figure, the 720 million visits, and the monetisation intent data have not been independently audited. Survey data from active users of a product inherently skews toward enthusiasts.

The $500 million ARR figure is a company claim based on annualising current monthly revenue, not confirmed by financial filings. Revenue run rate can decline as quickly as it grows, particularly in consumer and prosumer subscription businesses. The 146-employee figure raises its own question: whether a company can sustain enterprise-grade support, reliability, and security at this headcount as usage scales.

results.title: Lovable lève $400M  lors d’un tour de financement de série C, pour une valorisation de 13,3 milliards de dollars, le 12 août | Gate News
results.author: GateNews
highlights: Lovable, un créateur suédois d’applications d’IA, a levé 400 millions de dollars lors d’un tour de financement de série C le 12 août, portant la valorisation de l’entreprise à 13,3 milliards de dollars, selon son annonce officielle. Le tour a été mené par Menlo Ventures et codirigé par le Scaleup Europe Fund, géré par EQT. Fondée en 2023 par son PDG, Anton Osika, et son directeur technique, Fabian Hedin, Lovable a déclaré que ses utilisateurs avaient créé plus de 60 millions de projets depuis son lancement en novembre 2024 et que les applications développées sur sa plateforme enregistraient plus de 900 millions de visites par mois. L’entreprise prévoit d’utiliser ces fonds pour élargir son offre de produits, développer ses infrastructures et renforcer ses effectifs, avec pour objectif d’atteindre environ 450 employés répartis entre Stockholm, Londres, Boston, San Francisco et New York.
